citation.title: Toward Large Language Model-Driven Symbolic Topology Optimisation for Rapid Structural Concept Generation in Manufacturable Design
citation.venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing 10(4), 117
citation.version_coded: version of record, publisher PDF host

included.physics: multiphysics: structural elasticity, heat conduction, compliant mechanism; also fluid flow

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the cantilever benchmark, the language-model design attains 87.5% of the stiffness of the SIMP reference design.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 4.2's secondary generic per-iteration comparison: about 5 s for traditional TO / approximately 1.5 s for LLM topology generation = approximately 3.33. It is not a measured end-to-end cantilever speed-up.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and Section 4.2: thermal performance is about 94.3% of SIMP. Section 4.2: LLM iteration about 1.5 s versus conventional TO about 5 s. Sections 4.1 and 6 qualitatively claim less computational cost.

baseline.hardware_ml: 24-core Intel Core i7-13700 CPU, 64 GB RAM; NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, 96 GB GDDR7 (Section 4 opening)
baseline.classical_time: Around 5 s per iteration for traditional TO, cited generically for thermal example (Section 4.2); no cantilever baseline time stated
baseline.ml_time: Approximately 1.5 s per iteration for thermal topology generation (Section 4.2); no cantilever total time stated
baseline.quality_metric: Normalized stiffness relative to SIMP (Section 4.1, Figure 7); paper describes symbolic objectives and heuristic indicators rather than FE analysis of returned design
baseline.quality_gap: Cantilever LLM stiffness 0.875 versus SIMP 1.0, a 12.5% deficit (Section 4.1, Figure 7)

R1.evidence: Abstract's first quantitative classical comparison is stiffness, so the primary outcome does not compare speed.

R2.evidence: Abstract and Figure 7 compare quality; no baseline speed enters the primary outcome.

R3.evidence: The primary comparison in the abstract is stiffness, not amortized speed.

R4.evidence: Sections 3 and 4.1 assess the returned topology through symbolic or geometric objective indicators; the paper does not describe FE analysis of the returned cantilever design to verify its normalized stiffness against SIMP.

reporting.n_test_cases: 5 application cases: cantilever, heat sink, thermofluid channel, compliant mechanism and 3D structure (Section 4)

notes: The abstract gives a quantitative quality comparison before its qualitative cost claim, so the primary outcome follows the protocol's quality stratum. Fluid-flow example is ancillary; the primary cantilever comparison is in scope. The paper does not identify the SIMP implementation or describe a paired timing experiment for it.
